text:
maria: FYI saw a regression on staging after enabling AWQ+fp8 kernels — peak GPU mem up ~22% and 2x OOMs on long-chat traces. Repro script and profiler attached below. anyone seen KV cache dtype cause this?

sam: ugh, thanks for flagging. can you paste the profiler snapshot? sequence len, batch, kv dtype? :thinking: 

maria: repro: batch=4, seq=2048 (user history), model=redwood/open-awq-gptq, quant=AWQ, kv_dtype=float32 (we set it globally to be safe). profiler snippet: 
```
Peak GPU memory: 17.4 GB
Allocated (model weights): 6.2 GB
KV cache: 7.8 GB
Workspace (attention kernels): 2.6 GB
Fragmentation: 0.8 GB
Time: 1.9s / forward
```

maria: also saw many small alloc/free churns in timeline around attention calls.

chen: kv_dtype=float32 will kill you for long sequences. AWQ saves weight mem but if KV is float32 you'll blow up. switching kv to fp16 should drop ~half the KV footprint. we did that in a branch and peak dropped ~9GB.

alex: +1 but note FP16 + fp8 weights can trigger mixed-precision kernels that allocate large fp32 accumulation buffers for stability (accum buffers live in workplace). that's probably your workspace number. some fused attention kernels avoid that but others allocate temporaries proportional to seq_len * head_size.

ryan: also batching heuristics matter: our dynamic batcher was combining long-history requests (seq~1k+) into one GPU batch. more demographic: it merged 2 x 1k -> batch=2 seq=2k effective. heuristics should splinter long-history queries to avoid huge workspace peaks. we have a config flag: max_effective_seq_for_batching.

sam: good call. maria, can you post the runtime config? curious about allocator settings (reuse buffers / max_workspace_bytes).

maria: config dump: 
```
allocator: redwood_gpu_cached
allocator.max_reuse_blocks: 256
allocator.max_workspace_bytes: 268435456  # 256MB
buffers.reuse: true
kernels.attention_prefer_fused: auto
batching.max_effective_seq_for_batching: 1536
kv.default_dtype: float32
mixed_precision.accum_fp32: true
```

chen: allocator.max_workspace_bytes=256MB seems low — kernels then fall back to generic slower paths that sometimes allocate many small temporaries (fragmentation). paradoxically lowering max_workspace can increase peak fragmentation. try raising to 1GB for the short term and set kv.default_dtype=float16 for staging to test.

alex: for kernel selection: set kernels.attention_prefer_fused: true for short seq and set a dynamic fallback to streaming attention for seq > 1024. sample pseudo: 
```
if seq_len <= 512: use fused_attention
elif seq_len <= 1024: use block_fused_attention
else: use streaming_attention (low workspace, slightly higher compute)
```
this keeps workspace bounded.

ryan: also, enable buffer reuse scavenger sweep interval to reduce fragmentation: 
```
allocator.reuse_scavenge_interval_ms = 1500
allocator.max_reuse_age_ms = 60000
```
That got us stable on other models.

maria: ran quick experiment: set kv.default_dtype=float16 + allocator.max_workspace_bytes=1073741824 (1GB) + batching.max_effective_seq_for_batching=1024. result: peak GPU mem 9.1GB (was 17.4GB), forward 2.1s -> 1.95s, no OOMs on 10 runs. promising.

sam: nice! can you post the perf regression profile when you switched to fp16? any quality regressions?

maria: perf: 
```
Peak GPU memory: 9.1 GB
Weights: 6.1 GB
KV cache: 3.9 GB
Workspace: 0.8 GB
Fragmentation: 0.3 GB
Time: 1.95s / forward
```
Quality: quick token-level checks fine, we'll run evals.

chen: sounds like main issue was kv_dtype + aggressive batching combo. quantization nuance: AWQ stores weights tighter but some attention kernels expect float accumulators; ensure mixed_precision.accum_fp32 remains true to preserve numerics but avoid global float32 KV.

alex: edge-case: GPTQ variants sometimes require FP32 KV to avoid degenerate rounding when using layernorm in some fused kernels. add a model-level override: model_kv_dtype_overrides = {"gptq-ish-model": "float32"} and assert only for short seq. we should warn on >512 seq and force fp16.

ryan: tracking action items: 
- maria: run full eval suite on fp16-KV branch and smoke long-chat traces (owner: maria)
- sam/alex: add kernel selection policy + tests for streaming atten fallback (owner: alex)
- chen: add check in model-onboard pipeline to recommend kv_dtype based on expected max_seq 
- infra: experiment with raising allocator.max_workspace_bytes default from 256MB -> 512MB (owner: sam)

maria: doing the eval now. also found a hotspot: attention kernel chooses GEMM variant that allocates an extra scratch buffer when head_size % 64 != 0 — fragmentation + small-block churn. I'll log a bug with a repro.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout/kv-fp16-staging (maria) -> staging (canary 10%) @ 2025-04-12T17:12:30Z

sam: thanks everyone. if this stabilizes, we should add an automated alert when kv/cache > 40% of GPU mem to catch bad overrides early. :eyes: 

maria: agreed. will follow up with eval results in this thread. :thumbsup:
